About the Director Ravii Srivatsaa 🎥

Cinema is not just a job, it's My passion - Ravii Srivatsaa

Ravii Srivatsaa is an Indian film writer and director who has been actively involved in the Kannada Film Industry (KFI) for the last 29 years. He began his career as a writer with the film "Hello Daddy," starring the legendary actor Dr. Vishnuvardhan. Over the years, he has gained recognition for his work as a writer, contributing to films such as "Lady Police," "Karnataka Suputra," "Agni IPS," "Jackie Chan," "Naxalite," "1Man Army," "Law n Order," "Underworld," "Kichcha," "Yajamana," "Kotigobba," "Sye," "Election," "Maanikya," and "Vishnu Priya," among others. He has also worked on the screenplay and dialogue for 63 films.

In 2001, Ravii Srivatsaa received the "Best Writer" award from the Indian Medical Association for his work in the film "Yajamaana."

In 2005, he made his directorial debut with the realistic cult genre film "Deadly Soma," which earned him the 2005 Chennai Film Fans Association Award for Best Debutant Director.

Some of his notable directorial works include "Deadly Soma" (2005), "Ganda Hendathi" (2006), "Rajeev Gandhi" (2007), "Madesha" (2009), "Deadly 2" (2010), "Dashamukha" (2013), and "TigerGalli" (2017)

He has been dedicated to the Kannada Film Industry for the past 29 years, driven by his love for the craft.
